messages:
marta: heads-up — after the kernel selector change in today's canary deploy we're seeing intermittent OOMs on p4d nodes for the chat-16k model. Started ~10:02. Dump attached in thread (stack traces + allocator logs).

sam: saw it too, repro on a small traffic slice. Memory spike happens when sequence length > 6k and batch size coalesces to 12. Kernel switch seems to pick the 'fused_attn_v2' path which increases temporary workspace usage.

jin: any profiling traces? can we get per-kernel alloc peaks?

marta: yes — quick snippet from profiler: 
```
2026-03-18T10:03:45Z kernel=fused_attn_v2 peak_workspace_mb=3620
2026-03-18T10:03:46Z kernel=attn_blocked_v1 peak_workspace_mb=1180
allocator.free_failures=3
kvcache.eviction_rate=0.04
```

lee: interesting — fused_attn_v2 gives latency wins normally but uses ~3x workspace for long sequences. That explains OOMs.

anka: mitigation proposal we can roll immediately: 1) circuit-breaker on kernel selector: if estimated workspace > node_headroom -> force fallback kernel (attn_blocked_v1). 2) request-shaper: cap batch coalescing for chat-16k to max_batch=8 for the next 30m. 3) aggressive KV cache trimming for long-seq requests (drop non-prefix entries). 4) fallback route to quantized-16k model if headroom still exceeded.

sam: agree. add a temporary autoscale boost + disable continuous batching for the canary group while we validate. Also flag a perf alert for latency regressions.

marta: implementing circuit-breaker rule now: updating kernel_selector config to include headroom check and explicit fallback list. Pushing a soft rollout (10% of canary) at 10:12.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kernel_selector-v3 -> canary(10%) by marta at 2026-03-18T10:12:15Z

ops-bot: alert created: ENG-RUNTIME-2181502468 - OOM spikes on chat-16k, severity=high. Pager set for on-call.

lee: quick checklist for on-call if OOM persists: 
- enable kernel selector hard-fallback to attn_blocked_v1 globally (manual flip)
- reduce max_batch to 4 for worst-offending queues
- temporarily disable kvcache for that model (costly but safe)
- scale up dedicated pool by 2 nodes
- roll back kernel_selector-v3

jin: post-mortem actions we should record: 
- add workspace estimation to compilation path (precompute worst-case temp memory per kernel/seq_len)
- update kernel catalog with workspace metadata and quantized variant compatibility tags
- improve batch-coalescing heuristic to consider estimated workspace per candidate batch (not just request latency)
- add unit test for long-sequence workloads that asserts fallback triggers under headroom exhaustion

anka: immediate plan: 1) let the canary with headroom-check run 20m; 2) if no OOMs, increase to 50% and monitor; 3) if OOMs continue, flip global hard-fallback and roll back selector change. I'll coordinate with infra to pre-warm 2 nodes.

marta: canary steady for 8m with headroom-check; no new OOMs in that slice. latency +80ms on avg for forced fallback but throughput stable.

sam: create runbook snippet for support: include rollback command, kernel-selector toggle, request-shaper rule id, kvcache trim command. Keep it short.

lee: logging note — we should surface estimated_workspace and chosen_kernel in request traces for 30 days to help debug regressions.

anka: filed follow-up tickets: INF-2345 (workspace metadata in compiler), RTE-789 (batching heuristic change), SRE-1122 (runbook add).

marta: summary: immediate mitigation = kernel-selector headroom check + cap coalescing; outcome = prevented further OOMs in canary; next steps = implement estimation, update tests, add trace fields. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
